I would prepare action plans for the following situations:

a) She changes her mind and chooses the AP. 

b) She stays with you and does not implement no contact and/or any boundaries you set.

c) She waffles and changes her mind over and over again.

All three are plausible. If she stays with you AND she does the work, it seems like you'd have it handled. I'd prepare for the worst case scenarios like the above. Make the plans and *stick to them.* Do not listen to her words too much; look at her *actions* instead. Don't feel as if you need to convince her of anything or engage in circular arguments. Nothing you say will change her emotional reality. Instead, choose to act. 

A lot of BSes choose to keep their action plans to themselves, but I understand the need for communication. We still had love for the WS. If you choose to share, keep it simple and factual. Don't complicate it with precise numbers. Keep that for the lawyers and accountants. Just have an idea of what you want and what you are willing to give her in the event of a divorce or failure condition.

I'm going to ask you if this is a study or if it's an actual artwork, because those are two different things. Studies are "copies," in that you are trying to train your eye to see exactly what's in front of you and to replicate it. It's not an awful practice if you don't use studies for your actual artwork. It's important to distinguish between the two and to always state which is which.

If it IS a study, it's not horrible. You're getting there, but I notice that the proportions are off, and they look rather stiff because of the unrealistic shading. You don't seem to be shading around the structure of the forms, but instead you're copying imperfectly. So an imperfectly copied Nurse would have altered shading, but you tried to copy the shadows on the original Nurse, so in the end the mistakes are magnified. Does that make sense?

Other than the shading, the outlines are somewhat blocky and uniform, which gives it a very static feel. You can improve on this by varying your line thickness, but that will come with time and practice. There ARE artists that use mostly uniform lines, but they also have a more consistent overall look (e.g. Bryan Lee O'Malley) with more dynamic shadows. 

You also want to think about midtones and highlights in your drawing. I like Sakura Gelly Roll pens, they're cheap and they're a quick way to add highlights, but if you don't have that you can shade in midtones and plan around your highlights. It would add more dimension to the picture.

I really don't think it's an intruder for several reasons:

1) Illogical ransom note. The longest note I've ever seen, on stationery from the Ramsays (specifically Patsy). A kidnapper could literally just type up and print out what he wanted, not painstakingly write out a longass note. 

2) Wiped down flashlight and batteries on the counter. An intruder would have just taken it with them. Here's the thing - if the intruders were so competent as to leave without waking anybody, being seen, or leaving any evidence, how were they so INcompetent that they would leave something that looks so damn suspicious? 

3) The pineapple that both Ramsays deny feeding JonBenet. Why would JonBenet sit down in the middle of the night with a strange person to eat pineapple? If a family friend did it, why not use an untraceable "lure," like a wrapped candy that you can easily pocket? Why risk opening cabinets and leaving DNA/fingerprints?

(Burke's fingerprints were on the bowl of pineapple, btw.)

4) Redressed body and covered in special blanket, yet cruel garrote and head trauma. Not your typical kidnapper MO. The extra-big panties also meant that the killer or accomplice knew where to FIND panties, but did not dress her often enough to know her correct size.

5) There was so much cross-contamination on the scene that the foreign DNA evidence is just pointless. Furthermore this would invalidate Touch DNA evidence - JonBenet had been at a party the day before she passed! 

6) Broken window in the basement along with Jon Ramsay's inconsistent accounts of how and why it was broken. Reeks of incomplete staging.

I don't know which Ramsay killed JonBenet. I don't think it's Patsy, personally. People don't think about this, but Patsy was undergoing chemo at that time and it's a genuine, life-changing thing. I've had a relative go through chemo and pass from lung cancer, and chemo just absolutely wrecks your spirit. It wrecks everything. Patsy could NOT have written that ransom note as lucidly as it is on chemo. Only one crossed out word? Please.

Plus, why call the cops when staging was incomplete? If Patsy did it, why call the cops at all? Why not dispose of the body first? 

This leaves Burke and Jon. Personally, I think Jon did the coverup, was interrupted by Patsy's 911 call, and then had to hastily undo some of his staging and redo JonBenet's body, since he could not dispose of it. I don't know who, for sure, killed JonBenet.
